clue.text: Song added to after Pellinore's first exploit

indicators.note: first asks for just the opening letter of the knight's name that precedes it

parts.note: the initial of King Pellinore, an Arthurian knight
a lay is a ballad or narrative song
on as in tacked on, attached

explanation.surface: A medieval minstrel extends a ballad about a heroic deed of King Pellinore.
explanation.walkthrough: The song with something added comes after the knight's initial; 'exploit' looks like a noun for the deed but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To play on someone's fears or weaknesses is to take unfair advantage of them, the verb sense of exploit.

clue.text: Nonsense to have gold brought back from somewhere in Indonesia

parts.note: pap is worthless or trivial talk

indicators.note: brought back means carried the other way, so the symbol is read upwards from the bottom

parts.note: AU is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: Someone talks rubbish about bringing gold home from a trip to Indonesia.
explanation.definitionFit: Papua is the Indonesian province occupying the western half of the island of New Guinea, so it is one place within that country.

clue.text: Scoundrel taken in by song of a pastoral paradise

indicators.note: taken in by means received inside, so the rogue sits within the musical piece

parts.note: an aria is a solo song in opera
a cad is a man who behaves dishonourably

explanation.surface: A villain is fooled by a song celebrating an idyllic countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcadia, a region of ancient Greece, became the poets' byword for an idealised rural world of shepherds and simple happiness.

clue.text: Disgusting attack

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a military campaign of assault

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it sounds like a vile assault, but the two words are separate meanings, an adjective and a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective for something repellent and also a noun for an army's large-scale forward assault.

clue.text: Coolness shown by American doctor over practical joke? Not quite

indicators.note: not quite means falling just short, so the trick's word stops before its final letter

parts.note: A is a standard abbreviation for American
a ploy is a cunning trick or stratagem
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A calm US physician keeps a straight face while playing a prank.
explanation.walkthrough: The doctor ends up after the shortened trick, so 'over' is read loosely as a joining word; calling a ploy a practical joke is a stretch, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Aplomb is self-assurance and composure under pressure, which is what coolness means of a person's manner.

clue.text: Beat poet

definitions.meaning: first meaning: strike repeatedly and heavily
second meaning: Ezra, the American modernist writer of verse

explanation.walkthrough: 'Beat poet' suggests Ginsberg or Kerouac's movement, but the words split into a verb and a writer's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: To pound is to hit repeatedly, and Ezra Pound was a leading modernist American author of verse.

clue.text: Rejected as unfashionable by an exclusive social class say

parts.note: out as in no longer in vogue

indicators.note: say signals that the social group is to be heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: a caste is a closed hereditary social class

explanation.surface: Someone is snubbed by an elite clique for not being stylish enough.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcast is a person rejected or cast out by society, so the word works as an adjective meaning shunned.

clue.text: On the spot after a discontinuity in analysis of data

indicators.note: after tells us the immediate-payment word follows the gap word rather than leading

parts.note: a break is an interruption or gap
as in money down, paid immediately on the spot

explanation.surface: Something is noticed straight away following a gap in a statistical study.
explanation.definitionFit: A breakdown of figures divides them into categories so each part can be examined, a detailed analysis of the numbers.

clue.text: Stipulate extremely fiery ground spice at the outset

indicators.note: ground as in crushed in a mortar, so the seasoning's letters are broken up and remixed
at the outset places the crushed seasoning at the start, before the end letters

parts.note: the word spice, rearranged

indicators.note: extremely points to the two extreme ends of the word it qualifies

parts.note: the first and last letters of fiery

explanation.surface: A recipe insists that a hot, freshly ground spice goes in first.
explanation.definitionFit: To specify is to state a requirement precisely, which is what stipulating a condition does.

clue.text: A couple of statues in Parisian museum that should not be missed

indicators.note: in means sitting inside, so the pair goes within the gallery word

parts.note: musée is French for museum

indicators.note: a couple of means two, so just the first pair of letters is wanted

parts.note: the opening two letters of statues

explanation.surface: A pair of sculptures in a Paris gallery are said to be essential viewing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something billed as essential viewing, an attraction you are urged not to skip, is called a must-see.

clue.text: Sketch showing Dean and Lee with it in ruins

indicators.note: in ruins means wrecked and fallen apart, so the names and pronoun are broken and rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A drawing depicts two men, Dean and Lee, amid a wrecked scene.
explanation.definitionFit: To delineate is to trace an outline or describe precisely, as an artist does when making a quick drawing.

clue.text: Cape seen on female servant in French town

indicators.note: seen on means coming after in the line, so the headland follows the rest

parts.note: a maid is a female domestic servant
en is the French for in
a head or headland is a cape on a coast

explanation.surface: A cloak is worn by a housemaid in a provincial French town.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites a French town, but 'French' only supplies the word for 'in' and the town is English.
explanation.definitionFit: Maidenhead is a market town on the Thames in Berkshire, west of London.

clue.text: Kahn animated by a symbol of life

indicators.note: animated means set in motion, so the surname's letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone named Kahn is stirred by an emblem of vitality.
explanation.definitionFit: The ankh is the looped cross of ancient Egypt, the hieroglyph representing eternal existence.

clue.text: One animal or another covering over the front of it

indicators.note: over means placed on top of, so the garment word comes before the single letter

parts.note: a coat is a covering, here a second one alongside the animal's skin

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter alone

parts.note: the first letter of it

explanation.surface: An animal, or perhaps a different one, has a blanket draped over its head.
explanation.definitionFit: The coati is a long-snouted, ring-tailed mammal of the raccoon family from the Americas.

clue.text: Be willing to assist British politician occupied by work and class

indicators.note: occupied by means filled by, so the short creative word moves inside the statesman

parts.note: Sebastian Coe, Olympic runner turned Conservative MP
op, short for opus, is a work
rate as in first-rate, a class or grade

explanation.surface: A busy British MP is kept occupied with his job and social standing.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Coe, the former Olympic champion, was a Conservative MP; 'work' goes inside his name and 'class' is added after.
explanation.definitionFit: To cooperate is to work together willingly and help, which is being ready to lend support.

clue.text: Concerned with something done when working

parts.note: in as in involved in, engaged with
an action is a deed, something done

explanation.surface: Someone is preoccupied with a task completed while on the job.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine or person in action is operating or functioning, so the phrase means while busy at work.

clue.text: Disparaging remark about false praise overwhelming son earlier

indicators.note: earlier puts this whole unit ahead of the preposition at the clue's start
overwhelming means engulfing, so the male child's letter is swallowed inside
false means not genuine, so the compliment's letters are faked into another arrangement

parts.note: the word praise, rearranged
S is the standard abbreviation for son
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Someone makes a snide comment about insincere flattery heaped on a son.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspersion is a damaging or derogatory comment, as in casting aspersions on someone's character.

clue.text: Arrive at a particular state without hindrance after power becomes absolute

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the arrival verb wraps around the rest

parts.note: as in come undone or come right
P is the symbol for power
a let is an obstruction, as in without let or hindrance

explanation.surface: Once power is unchecked, a nation slides into a certain condition unobstructed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without hindrance' reads as the legal phrase meaning freely; here 'without' means outside. Power precedes the obstruction inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Complete and absolute both mean total, utter, with nothing lacking, as in complete or absolute silence.

clue.text: Right to interrupt short-story writer over books of momentous significance

indicators.note: in a down entry over means sitting above, so the writer comes before the scriptures
to interrupt means to break into, so the abbreviation is placed inside the writer's name

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe, master of the short story
Rt is the abbreviation for right, as in Rt Hon
NT, the New Testament, is a collection of books

explanation.surface: A storyteller insists on the right to break into a discussion of weighty books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' looks like a shortening instruction but belongs to the writer's description; 'Right' gives two letters, not R.
explanation.definitionFit: Portent means ominous meaning or importance, as in an event of great portent, so it matches weighty significance.

clue.text: Severely criticise taking in a German fellow professing polytheism

indicators.note: taking in means absorbing within, so the criticism verb surrounds the other letters

parts.note: to pan is to review harshly
taken as written
G is the abbreviation for German; fellow is surface padding making the German a person

explanation.surface: A critic slates a German man for worshipping many gods.
explanation.definitionFit: Pagan describes religions outside the main world faiths, often worshipping several deities rather than one God.

clue.text: Ambitious target ultimately abandoned by boss

indicators.note: ultimately abandoned means the final letter is dropped from the aim word

parts.note: a goal is a target or aim
a head is the person in charge

explanation.surface: A boss gives up on a lofty objective in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A go-ahead firm or person is enterprising and keen to make progress, which matches being driven and aspiring.

clue.text: Deterioration from use in river

definitions.meaning: first meaning: damage caused by long service
second meaning: the ..., a river in north-east England flowing through Durham

explanation.walkthrough: The Wear flows through Durham and Sunderland in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Wear is the gradual damage things suffer through repeated handling, and also the name of an English watercourse.

clue.text: Subsequently discovering where patients may be found tucking into dessert

indicators.note: tucking into means going inside as well as eating, so the hospital rooms go within the pudding word

parts.note: afters is British slang for pudding
a hospital ward houses patients

explanation.surface: Later, a visitor finds hospital patients enjoying their pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: Afters is informal British for the dessert course; the hospital rooms sit after AFTER and before the final S.
explanation.definitionFit: Afterwards and subsequently are synonymous adverbs both meaning at a later time.

clue.text: Notice piece of redwood boarding on deck

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement or notice

indicators.note: boarding means climbing aboard, so the single letter gets inside the preposition

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a piece of the tree word is just one letter, its first

parts.note: the first letter of redwood

explanation.surface: Someone spots a plank of redwood used for a ship's deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deck' looks like a ship's floor, but it is the verb meaning decorate.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck is to decorate, as in deck the halls, so it is a synonym of embellish.

clue.text: Famous explorer died a libertine

parts.note: d is the abbreviation for died
a rake is a dissolute pleasure-seeker

explanation.surface: A celebrated adventurer is said to have ended his days a womaniser.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Francis Drake was the Elizabethan seaman who led the second circumnavigation of the globe.

clue.text: One without much experience meeting people of fashion from the east

parts.note: to have as in have a good time, experience

indicators.note: from the east means read leftwards in an across entry, so the society word runs backwards

parts.note: the ton was fashionable society

explanation.surface: A naive newcomer is introduced to stylish society types visiting from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One without much experience' looks like the definition, but experience belongs to the wordplay. The ton is an old word for high society.
explanation.definitionFit: The have-nots are the poor, people who possess little, in contrast to the wealthy haves.

clue.text: Similar article penned by doctor with great enthusiasm

parts.note: like means similar

indicators.note: penned by means enclosed as in a pen, so the article goes within the medic's letters

parts.note: MD, Doctor of Medicine
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A doctor eagerly writes up a comparable piece for a journal.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something like mad means doing it furiously and energetically, an informal idiom for vigour and keenness.

clue.text: Fellow needing no introduction gets wine in bulk

indicators.note: needing no introduction means the opening letter of the man is left off

parts.note: a man's name such as Rex standing for any fellow
tent is a dark red Spanish wine

explanation.surface: A famous man so well known he needs no introduction buys his wine wholesale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Needing no introduction' reads as fame but means beheading. The fellow is presumably a three-letter name ending -EX such as Rex; tent is an old word for Spanish red wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Extent means size or scale, as in the full extent of the damage, so it matches the magnitude sense of bulk.

clue.text: Nervous with anticipation for study into self-confidence in retirement

indicators.note: in retirement means withdrawing or going back, so the whole combination is read in reverse
into means going inside, so the room word sits within the self word

parts.note: ego is self-esteem
a den is a private study

explanation.surface: A retired person lacks the confidence to take up a new course of study and is jittery.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on edge means tense and jumpy, unable to relax while waiting for something to happen.
